header.title: About Me
header.subtitle: Systems engineer, distributed services architect, and continuous learner.

story_paragraphs: I'm Bharath Kumar, a Senior Software Engineer based in Bengaluru, India. I've been fascinated by software engineering, distributed systems, and modern AI for years—driven by the rush of cracking tough architectural problems, optimizing performance under heavy loads, and figuring out how far a system can scale.

Currently at Optum Global Solutions, I lead microservices engineering initiatives empowering over 850 healthcare providers and processing data for more than 500,000 patients annually. My day-to-day work centers around high-throughput services with C# .NET 8, Microsoft Azure, Azure Cosmos DB, and healthcare interoperability standards like FHIR.

Beyond day-to-day engineering, I love digging into database internals—analyzing LSM-tree compactions, latch-free B-tree variants, tail-latency mitigation in multi-tenant cloud storage, and consensus protocols. I actively read and summarize academic literature to bridge theory with production architectures.

focus_areas.title: Distributed Backend Architecture
focus_areas.description: Designing decoupled microservices, event-driven pipelines, and high-throughput APIs with fault isolation.

focus_areas.title: Cloud & Database Internals
focus_areas.description: Leveraging Azure Cosmos DB, partition-level failovers, query optimization, and low-latency storage engines.

focus_areas.title: Performance Engineering
focus_areas.description: Tuning p99 tail latencies, load testing with JMeter, and eliminating architectural bottlenecks.
